A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIST2Loss, with matching core equations, methods, and experiments despite the changed title. Their complete main text, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on regression, visual grounding, robotic manipulation, reward modeling, and image generation, including component ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and adds loss-weight sensitivity, MMLU retention, and random-distance control results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The distance-derived targets, cross-entropy plus KL objective, high-dimensional metrics, contrastive augmentation, and place-value weighting are retained. The multi-token procedure moves from v2 Section 2.3 to v3 Appendix A.2. The added RL interpretation and applicability qualifications do not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix C.2 adds MMLU evaluation to assess general-knowledge retention after reward-model fine-tuning. The original regression, grounding, manipulation, reward-modeling, and ImageNet generation coverage remains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original Tables 1–5 is unchanged. The new checks include an unfine-tuned backbone comparator on MMLU and a random-distance variant compared with Euclidean DIST2Loss and SFT in Tables 7–8.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a seven-value loss-weight sweep from 0.001 to 1.0, randomly assigned label distances, and MMLU testing of reward-fine-tuned models. These are additional experimental protocols; the retained benchmark experiments have no documented changes to their settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds three distinct diagnostic analyses: sensitivity to loss weight, catastrophic forgetting on an unrelated task, and dependence on a semantically meaningful metric. These substantially broaden validation beyond the retained component ablations, token-replacement illustrations, and qualitative error cases.

E5.justification: The v3 reproducibility statement explicitly characterizes results as based on single or limited runs, extending v2's computational-resource explanation. Five-seed regression summaries and ten-seed ablation means and standard deviations remain unchanged. No increased run counts or new statistical estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: New Tables 6–8 report loss-weight sweep accuracies of 75.6–85.3%, MMLU accuracies of 44.5% for the backbone, 42.8% for SFT, and 43.9% for DIST2Loss, and random-metric accuracy of 76.0% versus 85.3% with Euclidean distance. Tables 1–5 and the relocated detailed regression and RewardBench results retain their values.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2.3 adds the entropy-regularized reward-maximization objective and its Boltzmann optimum, linking distance-based targets to independently defined per-token rewards. This is a limited new mathematical argument; the existing method equations remain, and no new proof or learning guarantee is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal distance-supervision and data-efficiency claims remain essentially unchanged. The introduction and conclusion add the claim that DIST2Loss provides a closed-form alternative to entropy-regularized RL with per-token rewards, extending the claimed contribution beyond v2's formulation.

C2.justification: v3 Section 2.3 and Appendix A.1 substantially qualify applicability through token-wise reward independence and explain credit-assignment failures for structured multi-token objectives. Appendix B expands the asymptotic caveat with a practical-resource argument, while Appendix C adds interpretations about knowledge retention and metric validity. The earlier multi-token workarounds remain documented.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C.1 newly describes temperature selection relative to token-space scale and states that it was not tuned, although exact temperatures remain unspecified. Most implementation settings and hardware information are relocated from v2 Appendix A to v3 Appendix D. Both versions promise future code release.

R1.justification: v3 adds Haarnoja et al. (2017) to connect DIST2Loss with entropy-regularized policy optimization. References to Kullback and Leibler, Williams and Zipser, and Geman et al. are removed. The main related-work categories and relationships to existing experimental methods remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, rewrites substantial introductory and concluding passages, and reorganizes the method around the RL connection. Multi-token material moves into an expanded appendix structure, and ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements replace the earlier checklist-based presentation. This is substantial narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The combined overview in v2 Figure 1 becomes two redesigned figures in v3. The regression plot is restyled, result tables receive new highlighting, the detailed regression table is restructured, and several appendix displays move. Three diagnostic tables are added alongside document-wide conference-format changes.

improvement.justification: The added controls in Appendix C address previously untested questions about metric validity, hyperparameter sensitivity, and knowledge retention, while clearer applicability limits and reorganized displays improve usability. Gains are limited by sparse protocol and uncertainty reporting. The sensitivity interpretation also overstates robustness: despite claiming drops occur only at small loss weights, Table 6 shows substantial drops at 0.2 and 1.0. The core method and benchmark results remain unchanged.
